headline: Cipla and Teva win USFDA approval for first generic Flovent HFA in 110 and 220 mcg strengths
dek: The companies say the jointly developed fluticasone inhaler is the first generic equivalent in these two strengths, in a US market they put at about $350 million.
body:
Cipla and Teva have received US Food and Drug Administration (USFDA) approval for a jointly developed generic version of Flovent HFA, according to a post on X summarising a Cipla filing. The fluticasone inhaler was approved through an abbreviated new drug application (ANDA) in 110 mcg and 220 mcg strengths. The companies describe it as the first generic equivalent in these two strengths.

The companies, citing IQVIA data as reported by Business Upturn, put the US market for these strengths at about $350 million. The post's author said they had not seen the FDA's own listing.

The post also noted that GSK discontinued the brand Flovent HFA at the end of 2023. A generic version of the 44 mcg strength, made by a different company, was approved earlier in 2026, according to the post.

The post cited the Cipla filing, Business Upturn and GoodRx as its sources.
key_quote: first generic equivalent in these two strengths
